newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia has no plans to award more power deals.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia has no plans to award more power deals.

text.p: Malaysian Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Thursday that there was no immediate plans to award any contract for power generation and distribution.
He told reporters after an official function that state utility firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd will remain the dominant player in the power industry.

There have been concerns that Tenaga may have lost its distribution monopoly after the government this week awarded a licence to generate and distribute electricity to a company for a high-technology park in northern Kedah state.
Moggie said the project in the Kulim area "doesn't undermine the position of Tenaga as the dominant power player".
The government has also not identified any other projects where independent companies will generate and distribute power, Moggie said.
He added that this could change in the future. "The next time we don't know...but immediately, no," he said.

Responding to a question whether there has been a shift in government policy after the award of the power generation and distribution contract for the Kulim project, he said: "Basically there is no shift in government policy".
"We do not anticipate that Tenaga will lose the dominant role. The demand for electricity will continue to grow. Tenaga will maintain its dominance for many years to come," Moggie said.
He said Malaysia's electricity needs will grow in the future, and that new independent power producer licences may be issued.
Tenaga will be allowed to bid in the construction of the new private power plants.
Tenaga stock had fallen 1.30 ringgit in the last two days on concerns that Tenaga may lose its electricity distribution monopoly. At 0200 GMT on Thursday, the stock was up 40 cents at 12.00 ringgit.
